failure_summary.description: Answers followed a related or salient context match instead of the clue’s requested category or defining relation, despite existing target-selection rules.
Answers mismatched the expected canonical form: one expanded a surname to a full name, and one gave only part of a work’s title.
The rank clue required counting successive advancement steps and returning the requested scout designation.

patch.reasoning: The skill already covers identifying the clue’s target and using the whole clue, so repeating those rules would not address the ignored-target failures. These edits clarify the ambiguous bare-place case, distinguish a full-title request from an explicit fill-in-the-blank, and add a general rule for counting rank progressions.

edits.target: When a prompt consists only of a place name, do not simply repeat it. If context clearly identifies its jurisdiction or location, treat the prompt as an elliptical request for that place attribute and answer with the supported information. Do not infer a relation when context does not make one clear.
edits.content: When a prompt consists only of a place name, do not simply repeat it. Treat it as an elliptical request for the place’s country or administrative location only when context supports that relation. For a city, give the country or jurisdiction stated in context, not a component of its formal style or name, unless the prompt asks for its formal name or status. Do not infer a relation when context does not make one clear.

For clues about advancing through an ordered series of ranks, count each successive rank after the stated starting rank to find the endpoint. Then match the requested answer slot: a clue asking who someone becomes or for “one of these” calls for the person or member designation, not merely the rank label.

When a clue asks for a named work but gives only a fragment of its title, return the complete conventional title, including the words already supplied by the clue. Return only the omitted word or words when the prompt explicitly asks to complete a blank or fragment.
